concepts.title: What is Science?
concepts.definition: Science is a way of understanding the world through careful observation, asking questions, and exploring how things work.
concepts.key_idea: Science begins with curiosity and careful observation of the world around us.
question_patterns: What is science?
How does science help us understand the world?
What are the three main activities that science involves?
Why is observation important in science?
Give one example of how science answers a question about daily life.

solution_steps.explain: Recognise what we want to understand about the world.
Use our senses and tools to gather information about the object or event.
Connect the observations to a scientific idea that helps us understand the world.

worked_examples.question: What is science in one sentence?
worked_examples.solution: Science is a way of understanding the world around us through observation, questioning, and exploration.
worked_examples.answer: Science is a way of understanding the world through observation, questioning, and exploration.

worked_examples.question: How does science help us understand why the sky is blue?
worked_examples.solution: We observe the sky, ask why it is blue, and explore how sunlight scatters in the air. Science explains this through scattering of light.
worked_examples.answer: Science helps by observing, questioning, and exploring to find that air scatters blue light.

exercises.question: Write one sentence explaining what science is.
Name two activities that science involves.
Give one example of a question science can help answer.

concepts.title: The Scientific Method
concepts.definition: A step-by-step process scientists use to answer questions: observation, hypothesis, experiment, and conclusion.
concepts.key_idea: The scientific method turns curiosity into reliable answers through a structured process.
question_patterns: What are the steps of the scientific method?
What is a hypothesis?
How does an experiment test a hypothesis?
Why is a conclusion important in the scientific method?
Give one example of using the scientific method.

solution_steps.explain: Notice something interesting and form a clear question about it.
Make a guess called a hypothesis and test it with a fair experiment.
Look at the results and decide whether the hypothesis is supported or needs to change.

worked_examples.question: List the four main steps of the scientific method in order.
worked_examples.solution: The steps are observation, hypothesis, experiment, and conclusion.

worked_examples.question: A student sees plants growing taller near a window. State a hypothesis they could test.
worked_examples.solution: A possible hypothesis is: plants grow taller when they get more sunlight.
worked_examples.answer: Plants grow taller when they get more sunlight.

worked_examples.question: Why is a conclusion needed after an experiment?
worked_examples.solution: A conclusion tells us whether the results support the hypothesis, so we know what we learned.
worked_examples.answer: A conclusion tells us whether the hypothesis is supported by the results.

exercises.question: What is a hypothesis?
Why must an experiment be fair?
Write the four steps of the scientific method in order.

concepts.title: Importance of Science in Daily Life
concepts.definition: Science helps us solve everyday problems and improve health, agriculture, transport, and communication.
concepts.key_idea: Scientific knowledge makes daily life safer, healthier, and more convenient.
question_patterns: How is science useful in daily life?
Give one example of science in cooking.
How does science help in keeping us healthy?
Why is science important for farmers?
Name one way science improves transport.

solution_steps.explain: Pick an everyday task such as cooking, farming, or travelling.
Determine which scientific idea or tool makes the activity work.
Describe how the science makes the activity safer, faster, or better.

worked_examples.question: Give one example of science in cooking.
worked_examples.solution: Heating water to boil rice uses the science of heat transfer, which cooks the food safely.
worked_examples.answer: Heat transfer lets us boil rice safely.

worked_examples.question: How does science help keep us healthy?
worked_examples.solution: Science gives us knowledge about germs, vaccines, and clean water, which prevent disease.
worked_examples.answer: Knowledge of germs, vaccines, and clean water prevents disease.

exercises.question: Name one way science helps farmers.
How does science improve communication?
Give one example of science in your home.

concepts.title: Science and Technology
concepts.definition: Science is the study of how things work, while technology applies scientific knowledge to make useful tools and devices.
concepts.key_idea: Technology uses scientific discoveries to solve practical problems.
question_patterns: What is the difference between science and technology?
Give one example of technology that uses science.
How does science lead to new technology?
Why is technology important in daily life?
Name one device that came from scientific discovery.

solution_steps.explain: Find the scientific idea or discovery involved.
Find the tool or device that applies that science.
Show how the scientific knowledge was used to build the technology.

worked_examples.question: What is the difference between science and technology?
worked_examples.solution: Science studies how things work; technology uses that knowledge to make useful tools.
worked_examples.answer: Science studies how things work; technology applies it to make tools.

worked_examples.question: Give one example of technology based on science.
worked_examples.solution: A torch uses the science of electricity and batteries to produce light.
worked_examples.answer: A torch uses electricity and batteries to produce light.

exercises.question: Name one technology in your classroom.
How did the science of flight lead to technology?
Give one example where technology solved a problem.

concepts.title: Curiosity and Scientific Temper
concepts.definition: Curiosity is the desire to ask questions and find out why things happen; scientific temper means thinking logically and checking evidence before believing.
concepts.key_idea: A curious and evidence-based mind is the foundation of science.
question_patterns: What is curiosity?
What does scientific temper mean?
Why is curiosity important for a scientist?
How can we develop scientific temper?
Give one example of thinking with scientific temper.

solution_steps.explain: Recognise something you want to understand or explain.
Ask questions and look for evidence rather than guessing.
Decide what to believe based on observations and facts.

worked_examples.question: What is scientific temper?
worked_examples.solution: Scientific temper means thinking logically and checking evidence before accepting any claim.
worked_examples.answer: Thinking logically and checking evidence before believing.

worked_examples.question: Give one example of using scientific temper.
worked_examples.solution: Before believing that a home remedy cures a cold, you check whether evidence supports it.
worked_examples.answer: Checking evidence before believing a home remedy cures a cold.

exercises.question: Why is curiosity important in science?
How can you develop scientific temper?
Give one example of asking a curious question.

concepts.title: Branches of Science
concepts.definition: Science is divided into branches such as physics, chemistry, biology, and earth science, each studying a different part of nature.
concepts.key_idea: Different branches of science study different aspects of the natural world.
question_patterns: Name three branches of science.
What does biology study?
What does physics study?
Which branch of science studies living things?
Give one example of a question chemistry tries to answer.

solution_steps.explain: Decide what the question is about, such as living things or forces.
Find which branch of science studies that topic.
Give an example that shows what that branch studies.

worked_examples.question: Name three branches of science.
worked_examples.solution: Three branches are physics, chemistry, and biology.

worked_examples.question: Which branch of science studies living things?
worked_examples.solution: Biology studies living things such as plants and animals.

worked_examples.question: What does physics study?
worked_examples.solution: Physics studies forces, energy, light, and motion.

exercises.question: What does chemistry study?
Name one branch of science and what it studies.
Which branch studies the Earth and its rocks?

concepts.title: Science as a Collaborative Adventure
concepts.definition: Science is done by people working together across countries and generations, sharing ideas and building on each other's discoveries.
concepts.key_idea: Scientists around the world and across time work together to build knowledge.
question_patterns: Why is science called a collaborative adventure?
How do scientists share their work?
Why is sharing discoveries important in science?
Give one example of scientists working together.
How does science grow over generations?

solution_steps.explain: Find a scientific idea or invention.
See which scientists contributed over time.
Show how sharing and building on ideas led to the discovery.

worked_examples.question: Why is science called a collaborative adventure?
worked_examples.solution: Scientists across the world and across generations share ideas and build on each other's work.
worked_examples.answer: Scientists share ideas and build on each other's work across time and place.

worked_examples.question: Give one example of scientists working together.
worked_examples.solution: Many countries shared data and research to develop vaccines quickly.
worked_examples.answer: Countries shared research to develop vaccines.

exercises.question: Why is sharing discoveries important?
How does science grow over generations?
Give one example of collaboration in science.
